overall_diagnosis: Observed failures cluster around incomplete and inconsistent multi-hop retrieval/structured extraction for q1 (expected 11 employee IDs but only 8 returned, with run-to-run drift) plus weak product grounding/disambiguation (cross-product leakage between similarly named products/artifacts). A secondary recurring issue is output schema/type correctness (e.g., tokens emitted as strings instead of numeric). The single available skill, enterprise-artifact-search, should be strengthened to enforce exhaustive enumeration, determinism, stronger grounding, and pre-write schema validation. Avoid repeating the previously rejected/attempted “exhaustive retrieval pass” patch content verbatim; instead add complementary, higher-leverage guardrails (deterministic query plan, explicit stop conditions, count reconciliation, and schema/type validation).

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Despite existing anti-distractor and multi-hop intent, execution shows partial entity enumeration (missing IDs), inconsistent results across runs (non-deterministic search plan / premature stopping), and occasional cross-product contamination (CoachForce vs similarly named products). Additionally, the agent failed strict output typing (tokens as strings), indicating the skill does not sufficiently mandate a final schema/type validation step tied to the benchmark’s JSON outputs.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Update the skill with complementary (non-duplicate) guardrails beyond generic “search more”: (1) Deterministic retrieval plan: require a fixed sequence of sources and query variants (start from the explicitly named product’s canonical artifact/index; then follow only linked artifacts; only then broaden to global search) and record the exact queries used to reduce run-to-run drift. (2) Explicit stop condition for enumeration: do not finalize until a full “no-new-entities” iteration occurs AND a reconciliation step is done (compare people mentioned across doc header authors/reviewers, PR reviewers, meeting action items, and directory/metadata tables; if any source references an extra person not in the set, continue). (3) Stronger product-grounding contract: before extracting IDs, the subagent must state the target product identifier and reject artifacts whose product field/name does not match unless there is an explicit cross-link (URL/doc reference) from an in-scope artifact. (4) Reviewer/role disambiguation rules: meeting participants are NOT reviewers; require explicit reviewer signals first (PR review, “reviewed by”, approval records), then evidence-based contributors; always attach evidence pointers per ID. (5) Pre-write output validation checklist embedded in the skill: verify keys q1–q3 exist, list lengths are plausible vs evidence counts, IDs match directory pattern, and numeric fields (e.g., tokens) are emitted as numbers not strings; if validation fails, return NEED_MORE_SEARCH or a repair action instead of emitting partial JSON.
